topics: 🔔 The Divine Voice — why the Tosefta bothers to rule like Beit Hillel; Rabbi Yehoshua disregards a bat kol
🕯️ Beit Shammai's Havdala — proving a baraita is theirs, and the difference between a day's arrival and departure
🍷 Does Grace Need a Cup? — Beit Shammai's single cup, tasting, the minimum measure, and two tanna'im
🧼 Wash or Mix First? — dueling purity decrees about liquid on the outside of the cup
🧻 Cloth on the Table or Cushion? — second-degree impurity, teruma eaters, and washing being rabbinic
🧹 Sweep or Wash First? — crumbs, an olive-bulk, and the am ha'aretz attendant; Rav Huna's ruling
🔥 Bara vs. Boreh — Rava and Rav Yosef on the flame blessing; 'there are many lights in a fire'

overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Reasons Behind Each Dispute
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 52a–52b
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The Gemara works through the mishna's list of Beit Shammai–Beit Hillel meal disputes one by one. It first tests Beit Shammai's kiddush position against a baraita about havdala and answers that a day's arrival is unlike its departure. It then asks whether Beit Shammai even require a cup for Grace after Meals. The three purity disputes — washing before mixing, where to lay the cloth, and sweeping before washing — are each unpacked as competing rabbinic decrees, with Beit Hillel adding an 'alternatively' each time. The daf closes with Rava's spices-first custom, the meaning of bara versus boreh, and why spices of gentiles get no blessing.

slides.title: 🕯️ Do Beit Shammai Really Put the Day Before the Wine?
slides.subtitle: A baraita on havdala seems to have wine first — the Gemara must show it is Beit Shammai's, then explain it

nodes.content: ❓ Baraita: entering one's house at the end of Shabbat, one blesses wine, then light, then spices, then havdala. Wine precedes the day's blessing!
🤔 Maybe that baraita is Beit Hillel's? No — it puts light before spices, and only Beit Shammai hold that (per Rabbi Yehuda's Tosefta: the Houses dispute only light and spices).

🤔 Maybe it is Beit Hillel per Rabbi Meir? No — in our mishna (Rabbi Meir) Beit Hillel say candle, spices, Grace, havdala, but the baraita puts everything after Grace. So it is Beit Shammai per Rabbi Yehuda.
❗ Then the contradiction stands: kiddush — day before wine; havdala — wine before havdala.
✅ Beit Shammai distinguish: at the day's arrival, the earlier we bring it in the better; at its departure, the later we send it off the better, so Shabbat is not a burden on us.

callout.label: First, the Divine Voice:
callout.text: Why say the halakha follows Beit Hillel when a bat kol proclaimed it? Either the Tosefta was taught before the bat kol, or after it, following Rabbi Yehoshua, who said אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּבַת קוֹל — one disregards a Heavenly Voice.

slides.title: 🍷 Do Beit Shammai Require a Cup for Grace After Meals?
slides.subtitle: The mishna's 'only that one cup' is pressed from every angle

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: The mishna: if only one cup came after the meal, Beit Shammai bless the wine and then Grace. Doesn't that mean he drinks it and Grace has no cup?

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: No — he blesses over it and sets it down for after Grace.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: But the Master said one who blesses must taste!

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: But the Master said tasting it disqualifies it as a cup of blessing!

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: He tastes with his hand, or pours a little into another cup.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: But a cup of blessing needs a minimum measure, and he has reduced it! And the mishna says 'only that cup'!

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: The cup held more than the measure: not two cups, but more than one.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: But Rabbi Ḥiyya taught: Beit Shammai say he blesses the wine, drinks it, and then recites Grace!

lines.speaker: Conclusion
lines.text: Rather, two tanna'im differ about Beit Shammai's view.

slides.title: 🧼 Three Purity Disputes, Three Pairs of Decrees
slides.subtitle: Each House guards against a different impurity chain; the root is what each permits
rows: Wash hands, then mix — or mix, then wash?
Liquid on the outside of the cup may become impure from unwashed hands and then render the cup impure
Liquid on the hands may become impure from the (outside-impure) cup and render the hands impure
BS forbid using a cup whose outside is impure (decree due to drips); BH permit it — drips are uncommon. Alternatively: תֵּכֶף לִנְטִילַת יָדַיִם סְעוּדָה
Cloth on the table or the cushion?
On the cushion, its liquid may become impure and then render the hands impure
On the table, its liquid may become impure and render the food impure

BS forbid using a second-degree table (decree for teruma eaters); BH permit — teruma eaters are vigilant. Alternatively: hand-washing for ḥullin is not from the Torah, so better hands be impure than food
Washing first splashes the crumbs and ruins food
If the attendant is a scholar he already removed olive-bulk crumbs; smaller crumbs may be destroyed
BH forbid using an am ha'aretz attendant; BS permit it, so food may still be on the table

callout.label: Principles invoked:
callout.text: Hands have second-degree impurity, and a second degree makes a third in ḥullin only through liquids. A vessel does not render a person impure, nor another vessel. A vessel whose outside became impure through liquid: its outside is impure but its inside, rim, ear, and handles are pure. Rabbi Yoḥanan: crumbs less than an olive-bulk may be destroyed by hand.

slides.title: 🌿 Rava Blesses the Spices First
slides.subtitle: Rav Huna bar Yehuda visits Rava and is surprised; Rabbi Yehuda's version explains it

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rav Huna bar Yehuda sees Rava bless over the spices before the light
2️⃣ His objection: in our mishna both Houses put the candle first — Beit Shammai: candle, Grace, spices, havdala; Beit Hillel: candle, spices, Grace, havdala

3️⃣ Rava: that is Rabbi Meir's version. Rabbi Yehuda says the Houses agree Grace is first and havdala last, and dispute only light and spices — Beit Shammai: light then spices; Beit Hillel: spices then light
4️⃣ Rabbi Yoḥanan: the people practice like Beit Hillel according to Rabbi Yehuda — spices first

callout.label: Rav Huna's ruling on the chapter:
callout.text: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina in the name of Rav Huna: in this whole chapter the halakha follows Beit Hillel, except for the sweeping dispute, where it follows Beit Shammai. Rabbi Oshaya taught the mishna with the opinions reversed, so that here too the halakha follows Beit Hillel.

slides.title: 🔥 'Who Created' or 'Who Creates'? One Light or Many?
slides.subtitle: Two amora'im locate the real dispute in the flame blessing, then the spices of gentiles

boxes.title: Rava
items: The dispute is בּוֹרֵא: Beit Shammai — it means 'will create' (future); Beit Hillel — it also means 'has created'

boxes.title: Rav Yosef
items: Objection: 'Who forms light and creates [boreh] darkness' (Isaiah 45:7), 'forms mountains and creates wind' (Amos 4:13), 'creates the heavens' (Isaiah 42:5) — boreh clearly means past creation
So both words mean 'created'; the dispute is light vs. lights: Beit Shammai — one light in a fire; Beit Hillel — many lights (red, green, white)
Baraita: Beit Hillel told Beit Shammai, 'there are many lights in the fire'

boxes.title: Spices of gentiles
items: A gentile's candle: no blessing because it did not 'rest' on Shabbat — but why not their spices?
Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav: the mishna means a gentile party, which is presumed to be for idolatry
But the mishna's last clause separately bans idolatry's candle and spices! Rabbi Ḥanina of Sura: the mishna is giving the reason — gentiles' spices are banned because their parties are for idolatry

callout.label: Leading into the next daf:
callout.text: A baraita: over fire that 'rested' one blesses; over fire that did not rest one does not. The Gemara asks what 'rested' means — and the answer continues.

summary.principle: Each Beit Shammai–Beit Hillel meal dispute rests on a rabbinic decree about impurity or on a principle of order — frequent before infrequent, welcome the day early and see it out late.

flowSteps.content: 🔔 'Halakha follows Beit Hillel' — taught before the bat kol, or like Rabbi Yehoshua who disregards it
🕯️ Beit Shammai's havdala baraita (wine first) → arrival of the day is advanced, departure delayed
🍷 Do Beit Shammai need a cup for Grace? Set it aside, taste by hand, extra measure… Rabbi Ḥiyya's baraita → two tanna'im

columns.content: 🧼 Wash/mix, cloth, sweep: each House decrees against a different liquid chain; root = what each permits (impure-backed cup, second-degree table, am ha'aretz attendant)
🌿 Rava blesses spices first — Beit Hillel per Rabbi Yehuda; 'many lights in the fire'

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Rav Huna — the whole chapter follows Beit Hillel except sweeping before washing, where Beit Shammai prevail

quiz.q: How do Beit Shammai reconcile blessing the day before the wine in kiddush with blessing the wine before havdala?
o: They hold havdala is not a blessing over the day at all
The arrival of the day should be advanced as much as possible, while its departure should be delayed so Shabbat is not a burden
The havdala baraita is actually Beit Hillel's opinion
Wine is more frequent than havdala
quiz.e: After proving the baraita is Beit Shammai's (per Rabbi Yehuda), the Gemara answers that Beit Shammai distinguish between the entrance of the day, which we hasten, and its exit, which we postpone.

quiz.q: What is the Gemara's final answer to the challenge from Rabbi Ḥiyya's baraita, in which Beit Shammai bless the wine, drink it, and then recite Grace?
o: He tasted the wine with his hand
The cup contained more than the minimum measure
Two tanna'im disagree about Beit Shammai's opinion
Rabbi Ḥiyya's baraita follows Beit Hillel
quiz.e: The earlier answers (setting the cup aside, tasting by hand, extra measure) cannot explain a baraita that has him drink the wine, so the Gemara concludes there are two tannaitic versions of Beit Shammai's view.

quiz.q: Why, according to the Gemara, do Beit Shammai worry about liquid on the outside of the cup rather than the hands rendering the cup impure directly?
o: Because a vessel does not render a person impure
Because hands have second-degree impurity, and a second degree makes a third in ḥullin only through liquids
Because the cup is always full
Because washing hands for ḥullin is a Torah law
quiz.e: Unwashed hands are second-degree; they cannot render non-sacred items impure directly, only via liquids, which by rabbinic decree become first-degree.

quiz.q: In which dispute of this chapter did Rav Huna rule that the halakha follows Beit Shammai?
o: The order of kiddush
Whether to wash hands before mixing the cup
Whether to sweep the house before washing with the final waters
The wording of the blessing over fire
quiz.e: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said in the name of Rav Huna: in the whole chapter the halakha follows Beit Hillel except for sweeping before washing; Rabbi Oshaya reversed the opinions so that here too it follows Beit Hillel.

quiz.q: According to Rav Yosef, what do Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel actually dispute in the blessing over fire?
o: Whether bara refers to the past
Whether boreh refers to the future
Whether the blessing is recited at all on Saturday night
Whether a fire contains one light or many lights
quiz.e: Rav Yosef showed from verses that boreh means past creation, so the dispute is 'light' versus 'lights': Beit Shammai hold a fire has one light, Beit Hillel that it has many.
